ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{1}{x}$ intersects the sides AB and BC of the rectangle ABCO at points E and F, respectively, where points A and C are on the coordinate axes. If $AB=(n+1)AE$, what is the area of the quadrilateral OEBF?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect OB.\\
$\because$ AB=$(n+1)$AE\\
$\because$ BE＝nAE,\\
$\therefore$ S$_{\triangle OBE}$＝n$\cdot$S$_{\triangle OAE}$,\\
$\because$ E, F lie on y＝$\frac{1}{x}$ and quadrilateral AOCB is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore$ S$_{\triangle AEO}$＝S$_{\triangle OCF}$＝$\frac{1}{2}$, S$_{\triangle OBC}$＝S$_{\triangle OBA}$,\\
$\therefore$ S$_{\triangle OBE}$＝S$_{\triangle OBF}$＝$\frac{1}{2}$n,\\
$\therefore$ S$_{\text{quadrilateral}OEBF}$＝\boxed{n}.

If $AB=(n+1)AE$, what is the area of the quadrilateral $OEBF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect $OB$.\\ Because $AB=(n+1)AE$, we have $BE=nAE$.\\ Therefore, $S_{\triangle OBE}=n\cdot S_{\triangle OAE}$.\\ Because $E$ and $F$ lie on $y=\frac{1}{x}$ and $AOCB$ is a rectangle, we have $S_{\triangle AEO}=S_{\triangle OCF}=\frac{1}{2}$ and $S_{\triangle OBC}=S_{\triangle OBA}$.\\ Therefore, $S_{\triangle OBE}=S_{\triangle OBF}=\frac{1}{2}n$.\\ Hence, $S_{\text{quadrilateral }OEBF}=\boxed{n}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the coordinate system has O as the origin, the x-axis to the right, and the y-axis upward. In rectangle ABCO, O is at the lower-left corner, A is on the positive x-axis, C is on the positive y-axis, and B is the upper-right corner; therefore AB is the right vertical side, and BC is the upper horizontal side. The graph of the inverse proportional function y=1/x intersects the vertical side AB at E, and intersects the horizontal side BC at F. Reasoning: According to the coordinate method, let O=(0,0), A=(a,0), C=(0,b), B=(a,b), where a,b>0. Since E is on AB, the x-coordinate of E is a; also E is on y=1/x, so E=(a,1/a), hence AE=1/a. The given condition is AB=(n+1)AE, and AB=b, so b=(n+1)/a, that is, ab=n+1. Since F is on BC, the y-coordinate of F is b; also F is on y=1/x, so F=(1/b,b). Use the shoelace formula to calculate the area of quadrilateral OEBF, with vertices in order O(0,0), E(a,1/a), B(a,b), F(1/b,b). The area is 1/2[(0·1/a+a·b+a·b+(1/b)·0) - (0·a+(1/a)·a+b·(1/b)+b·0)] = 1/2[2ab-2] = ab-1. From ab=n+1, the area is n.
